To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we develop a parsimonious kernelized online learning algorithm that converges almost surely and that we establish the first online kernel learning method that can be applied to large scale datasets.

(1) we propose an online kernelized stochastic gradient descent method for function estimation in RKHS; (2) we develop a parsimonious projection scheme based on KOMP to approximate the resulting stochastic sequence; and (3) we prove convergence of the proposed method under both constant and diminishing step sizes.
(1) the proposed method is applicable to online learning with kernels, and that (2) it can be used to obtain parsimonious approximants of stochastic sequences of nonlinear function estimates in RKHS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel online learning algorithm for nonlinear function estimation that can be applied in large scale problems.
the development and analysis of a new algorithm for online learning in a reproducing Hilbert space.
the design and analysis of online kernel learning methods that overcome the computational and memory limitations of kernel methods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is a viable alternative to existing kernel based methods for online learning, and is applicable in a variety of settings.
the use of sparse projections in RKHS is a promising direction for online kernel learning.
the proposed method can be used for online learning with kernels, with computational and storage complexity that is linear in the dimensionality of the input space and the number of iterations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it provides a novel approach to kernelized online regression and classification, and establishes the first theoretical guarantees for the convergence of kernel methods in online learning.
we show that it is possible to learn nonlinear kernels in an online setting with a parsimonious memory requirement, and that this is done without any prior knowledge of the underlying function class.
the proposed algorithm achieves a linear convergence in the online kernel learning problem, and it is also competitive with the state-of-the-art in batch settings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
kernel methods can be used to learn in online setting without incurring a curse of kernelization.
the proposed online kernelized learning method can be used to efficiently learn a parsimonious approximation of the true underlying regression function.
the curse of kernelization can be alleviated by using a combination of sparse projections and stochastic approximation methods.
